Sam — thanks for the options and the CSV. Quick note on DST: the EU switches back to standard time on Sun Oct 25 this year, the US doesn't change until Nov 1, so anything scheduled in the last week of October can show a one-hour shift between EU and US. For Oct 13–16 we're safe, but worth calling it out if we want a recurring slot.

90 minutes sounds right. For Redwood, we can staff:
- Lead SE: Dylan Brooks (serving runtime + batching)
- Cover: Stephanie Nguyen (deploy/ops, will join for rollout/Q&A)

My preference is Option A (early US morning) because it gives Li a daytime slot and lets our APAC engineer sit in late-night if needed. To make it concrete, here are the UTC conversions for Option A (so calendar invites don't flip unexpectedly):
- Tue Oct 13, 16:00–17:30 UTC (09:00–10:30 PT / 17:00–18:30 CET / Wed 01:00–02:30 SGT)

If that matches Arcadia's choice we'll send a calendar invite with a Zoom link and a short runbook (what to bring: sample prompts, representative model sizes, spike dataset, and the engineer availability CSV).

Two logistical asks:
1) Can Arcadia add a brief list of goals for the 90 minutes (e.g., expected throughput target, latency SLO, data residency constraints)?
2) Is there any internal maintenance window Oct 12–16 we should avoid?

If Option A works, I'll send the invite. If you'd prefer Option B, let us know and we'll check calendars.

—Vanessa

- I have a morning (US) on-call handover on Tue Oct 13 at 09:30 PT that runs ~30m; I can shift the start by 15 minutes but not much.
- APAC attendance: our SRE (Nina, not cc'd) is in Singapore and prefers starting before 02:00 SGT; Option A's 01:00–02:30 SGT is borderline but she said she'd make the tail end if the meeting starts on time.

Proposal to keep the session useful: start at 09:15 PT / 16:15 UTC and keep strict timing (90 minutes max). That gives a 15-minute buffer for my handover and improves APAC's ability to join more of the session.

If that works for Arcadia we'll lock 16:15–17:45 UTC on Tue Oct 13 and I will publish a short agenda (runtime demo -> cache deep dive -> sizing table -> Q&A).
